provenance: Ground truth labelled by hand on 2026-09-05 from two detector failures David reported the same day. Timings are read from the aligned-STT cache entry the detector itself consumed, so a replay sees byte-identical input. No podcast prose or audio is stored here: each case points at a cache entry by sourceHash and the harness resolves it locally at run time. `audioDurationSeconds` is what the detector's own `probe_duration` saw: preparation overwrites the download in place, so it is derived as the cut file's measured duration plus the spans the run removed, rather than probed from an original that no longer exists.

labels.must-cut: Advertising. The detector is wrong if it leaves any of this in.
labels.must-keep: Programme content. The detector is wrong if it removes any of this. A failure here destroys something the listener wanted.
labels.acceptable-cut: Not advertising, but David has said he does not mind losing it. Neither cutting nor keeping is a defect; recorded so a replay does not score it either way.

cases.intentionalCondition: Two back-to-back produced pre-roll spots open the episode and neither was detected. The second one literally opens 'support for the show comes from Google Gemini'. A later Granola host read beginning 'for the show comes from granola' was also left whole. The detector returned three other correct spans, so these are misses, not mis-sizing.
cases.reportedBy: David, 2026-09-05: 'it opens with a deepgram.com ad and then a gemeini ad, neither were removed'; David, 2026-09-07: reported the Granola host read at 4066.16-4122.76 was not removed.

gaps.reported: Episode 1098 returned zero advertisements almost immediately. The backend had been constructed but never loaded, and every request failure was converted into 'not an advertisement'.
gaps.missing: The exact aligned-STT cache entry that run consumed is gone, so there is no input a replay could be scored against.
gaps.closes: Nothing labelled can close it: no judgement was ever made. The worker's explicit load, its counted failures and the `ads-backend-failed` refusal are what a unit test covers, and re-preparing the episode today would measure a different transcript.

gaps.reported: Concurrent preparations failed around model load, from speech-to-text and GGUF residency contending for the same GPU.
gaps.missing: There is no labelled audio that could express a scheduling failure; the corpus scores judgements, not admission.
gaps.closes: The shared admission lock and residency drain, under their own tests. Listed here so the inventory is not read as a list of unfixed detector defects.

gaps.reported: Episode 955's cuts drifted: the publisher transcript described a shorter advertising rendering than the audio actually carried, and similar duration was accepted as identity.
gaps.missing: The exact historical aligned-STT cache entry is gone. A dynamically inserted break is re-rolled per download, so re-fetching the episode does not recover the input that failed.
gaps.closes: Aligned-STT timing is now required for a destructive cut, which removes the mechanism. A labelled case would need a retained input with a documented dynamic insertion, which nothing on this machine has.

gaps.reported: A host read survived: the coarse pass called it conversation, and the spoken domain name lacked the spelling the anchor expected.
gaps.missing: No retained input for the episode has been identified, and no hand-timed interval exists for it.
gaps.closes: The cached input plus hand-timed advertising and programme boundaries. Until then the anchor-plus-CTA recovery is covered only by synthetic cues.

gaps.reported: A short produced Chase Sapphire spot was discarded by the sparse-run promotional-evidence gate, which did not recognise legal and brand copy as evidence.
gaps.missing: The input is retained -- sourceHash sha256:3a1051fa9b3c5c2bc85e450a3cd9cf150270d0a9859a3b9a38265a5e56c44961, 59 Parakeet 1.1B cues -- and the historical advertising interval 839.32-860.00 is documented. What is missing is bounded programme labels for the rest of the episode: a case with one must-cut and no must-keep would score a detector that cut the whole episode as perfect.
gaps.closes: Hand-timed programme boundaries around that interval, against the retained cache entry.

gaps.reported: A sister-show pitch split at a cue boundary: the call to action fell outside the sparse run that nominated it.
gaps.missing: Not an input gap but a policy one. Whether an unpaid house promotion for another show in the same network is advertising has not been decided, and labelling it either way would put a decision into ground truth that David has not made.
gaps.closes: An explicit owner decision on house promotion versus paid advertising. The `acceptable-cut` label exists for exactly this and is deliberately unscored.

gaps.reported: A nine-minute-twenty-three-second episode was overcut: two reads bracketed almost the whole news programme.
gaps.missing: The original short episode's input is unavailable. Other TechCrunch entries in the local cache are different episodes and cannot stand in for it; using one would be inventing the case.
gaps.closes: Proportional rejection and bounded resize cover the mechanism under synthetic cues. A labelled case needs a retained short episode with its own provenance.

gaps.reported: Coarse cue boundaries held advertising and real content in one cue, and a postroll was removed only in part.
gaps.missing: No retained input where a single cue is known to straddle the boundary has been identified. The corpus's two episodes do not exhibit it.
gaps.closes: A retained episode with a hand-timed intra-cue boundary. Until then the mixed-cue and postroll questions are covered only by synthetic cues.

gaps.reported: Two speech-to-text engines did duplicate work: the detector and the displayed transcript transcribed the same audio independently.
gaps.missing: Not expressible as a labelled case. It is an invariant about how many passes run, not about which seconds are advertising.
gaps.closes: Held by the worker's own tests and by this corpus consuming the cache rather than transcribing. A replay that transcribed again would break that invariant silently, which is why it is recorded here.

gaps.reported: An episode was labelled ready because a transcript or a downloaded file existed, not because preparation had completed.
gaps.missing: No labelling of audio could catch it; the defect is in what the app claims, not in which seconds were cut.
gaps.closes: The outcome contract between the worker and Swift, under its own tests.

gaps.reported: The app was replaced while a worker was running, leaving the job neither finished nor failed.
gaps.missing: Not a detector judgement. Bootstrap now marks interrupted jobs failed; an in-flight guard in the installer is still open.
gaps.closes: The installer guard, not a corpus case.
